quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #7
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks can you have before your driving is affected?
questions.correctAnswerText: One
questions.explanation: Do not drive after drinking any amount of alcohol. Even one drink affects your ability to drive safely.

questions.question: You can cross double yellow lines to pass another vehicle if:

options.text: The vehicle in front moves to the right to let you pass.
The yellow line on your side of the road is broken.
The yellow line on the opposite side of the road is broken.

questions.correctAnswerText: The yellow line on your side of the road is broken.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means traffic on that side can pass if it is safe. A solid yellow line means you cannot pass.

questions.question: Looking far ahead on the highway helps you:
questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid sudden braking or turning.
questions.explanation: Watch the road ahead and be ready to stop or change lanes. This helps you drive safely, save fuel, and keep traffic moving smoothly.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection, you must:

options.text: Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Let oncoming traffic and pedestrians yield to you.
Never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Left-turning drivers must yield to oncoming traffic. You must always yield to pedestrians.

questions.question: Driving too fast:

options.text: Helps you react faster to dangers.
Often leads to dangerous driving choices.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often leads to dangerous driving choices.
questions.explanation: Excessive speed is a major cause of crashes. It does not save time and often leads to dangerous driving decisions.

questions.question: Always stop before railroad tracks when:

options.text: You cannot completely cross the tracks before stopping.
The crossing is in a city with frequent trains.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot completely cross the tracks before stopping.
questions.explanation: A train can come at any time on any track. Make sure your vehicle fully clears the tracks before you stop. Do not stop on the tracks.

questions.question: Night driving is more dangerous because:

options.text: You cannot see as far ahead.
The road is always more slippery.
Your reaction time is always slower.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as far ahead.
questions.explanation: Poor visibility and headlight glare make it harder to see far ahead at night. Always use headlights and be extra careful in the dark.

questions.question: Use your horn when:

options.text: Another vehicle is in your way.
It can help prevent a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can help prevent a crash.
questions.explanation: Use your horn only to avoid crashes. Do not use it to tell someone to drive faster or move out of your way.

questions.question: This sign warns you of:
questions.correctAnswerText: A railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: A round sign warns of a railroad crossing ahead. Slow down, look, listen, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What helps reduce road rage?

options.text: Talk on your cell phone while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal when changing lanes.
questions.explanation: To prevent road rage, follow all laws and signals. Always signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: When driving on snow or ice:

options.text: Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.
Follow other vehicles closely for traction.
Pump your brakes to keep them from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.
questions.explanation: Use a low gear on steep hills to prevent skidding. Stay farther back from other vehicles than usual. Avoid quick stops. Unless you have antilock brakes, pump the brakes to slow down.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: The road curves left then right.
The road curves right then left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right then left.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs tell you what is ahead. This sign shows the road will curve right, then left. Slow down to safely follow the curves.

questions.question: When backing up:

options.text: Press hard on the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: Put your right arm on the passenger seat and look directly out the rear window. Mirrors do not show what is directly behind your vehicle. Back up slowly.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lines mean:
questions.correctAnswerText: No one can pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic going in opposite directions. Double solid yellow lines mean no passing from either direction.

questions.question: As you go faster, it is important to:

options.text: Look far ahead of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look far ahead of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds mean longer stopping distances. Look far ahead so you have time to safely react to hazards.

questions.question: How can you help keep the driver behind you at a safe distance?

options.text: Drive 10 mph faster than the car behind you.
Drive 10 mph slower than the car behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at a steady speed.
questions.explanation: Keep a safe distance by driving at a steady speed. Also signal before you turn, change lanes, or slow down.

questions.question: If oncoming headlights are blinding you at night, what should you do?

options.text: Look toward the right edge of the road.
Switch your lights to high beams.
Turn your lights on and off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: Look at the right edge of the road instead of staring at the headlights. This keeps your vehicle on the road safely until you pass the oncoming car.

questions.question: When should you allow extra space in front of your vehicle?
questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Leave extra space behind motorcycles. They can stop faster than other vehicles. You need room to stop if the motorcycle brakes suddenly or the rider falls. Motorcycles are also hard to see at night because they have only one tail light.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Upcoming intersection.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to watch for upcoming conditions. This sign warns you of an upcoming intersection so you can prepare to turn or watch for traffic.

questions.question: When must you use your low beams?
questions.correctAnswerText: In fog.
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off precipitation and create glare, making it harder to see. Many vehicles have fog lights that work with low beams.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Reserved parking for persons with disabilities.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter.
questions.explanation: This sign is posted on one-way streets and roads where you cannot enter. You may see it if you try to enter an expressway ramp the wrong way.

questions.question: Why should you increase your following distance behind a large vehicle?

options.text: To see around the sides of the vehicle.
Because other drivers tend to pull behind large vehicles before passing.
Because following too closely will trap you in the vehicle's slipstream.

questions.correctAnswerText: To see around the sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Drivers of trucks, buses, and vans may not see you if you are directly behind them. Extra space lets you see around the vehicle and see the road ahead.

questions.question: At night, an oncoming car has high beams on and you cannot see the road. What should you do?

options.text: Look toward the left edge of your lane.
Look toward the right edge of your lane.
Look straight ahead in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at the headlights. Instead, look toward the right edge of your lane and watch the oncoming car out of the corner of your eye.

questions.question: Water on the road can cause hydroplaning. At what speed can this happen?
questions.correctAnswerText: 35 miles per hour.
questions.explanation: At speeds up to 35 mph, tires push water away. Above 35 mph, tires cannot move water fast enough. Your tires lose grip and slide on the water like water skis.

questions.question: How can you avoid losing traction on wet roads?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Lower your speed on wet roads and keep your tires in good condition. If you lose control, ease off the gas. Do not brake hard. Keep the wheel straight and let the car slow down naturally.

questions.question: The road ahead is covered in heavy smoke. What should you do?

options.text: Turn on your four-way flashers and continue.
Slow down, move to the right as far as possible, and stop off the roadway.
Turn on your high beam headlights and continue.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move to the right as far as possible, and stop off the roadway.
questions.explanation: Slow down immediately. Move as far right as possible and stop off the road. Then decide if it is safe to continue. Some smoke can irritate your eyes and lungs or be dangerous to breathe.

questions.question: The traffic light turns yellow as you approach the intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to clear the intersection before the light turns red.
Come to a safe stop and wait for the green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a safe stop and wait for the green light.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the light is about to turn red. If you have not entered the intersection, stop safely. Speeding through a yellow light is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: When driving in a construction zone, what should you do?

options.text: Expect construction workers to yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Expect the unexpected.
questions.explanation: Construction zones have unexpected conditions. Drive with extra caution for your safety, other drivers, and construction workers.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spots?

options.text: By looking in your side mirrors.
By turning your head and looking over your shoulders.
By looking in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: By turning your head and looking over your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Turn your head and look over your shoulder to check them.

questions.question: Which factor affects how quickly a person absorbs alcohol?
questions.correctAnswerText: Weight
questions.explanation: A person's weight affects how fast they absorb alcohol. Other factors include biological sex and how much food they have eaten. The only way to remove alcohol from your system is to wait.
